title: Joint replacement decisions when frailty is already present (UK)

direct_answer: Frailty does not automatically rule out joint replacement, but it affects the risks and recovery. A shared decision with your surgical team should weigh benefits, risks and your goals. Prehabilitation, an anaesthetic assessment and planning for support at home can help.

content:
Hip and knee replacements can greatly reduce pain. For people living with frailty, the decision needs extra thought.

This guide covers questions to explore with your team. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Questions to ask

  • What benefits could I expect?
  • What are the risks for me?
  • How long is recovery, and what help will I need?
  • What happens if I wait or do not have surgery?

Anaesthetic risk and frailty

A pre-operative assessment checks your health and may identify ways to reduce risk. Frailty can increase the chance of complications such as delirium, so ask what support is in place.

Preparing for surgery

Prehabilitation, such as strength exercise and good nutrition, may help recovery. Plan equipment and support at home in advance.

Tablets, topical options and what not to DIY

While deciding, keep using pain relief as advised. Do not change medicines without advice, especially before surgery.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Am I too old for a joint replacement?

Age alone is not the deciding factor. Overall health and goals matter.

Can I change my mind?

Yes. You can ask for more time or a second opinion.
